data.name: Suren
data.long_meaning: The Armenian name Suren is derived from the Old Persian word 'sur', meaning 'ruler' or 'lord'. In Armenian history, the name was borne by several kings and princes, including Suren I (r. 330–345 AD), who is considered the founder of the Armenian kingdom of Artsrunik. Suren is also the name of a saint in the Armenian Apostolic Church, commemorated on May 23.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for those who are called to rule and lead with wisdom and strength.
data.numerology_meaning: A name with a 6 Life Path Number indicates that the person is nurturing and caring by nature. They are also responsible, loving, and creative.

in_greek.name: Σουρήν
in_greek.long_meaning: Σουρήν είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από τον Καύκασο, σημαίνει 'θώραξ' ή 'ασπίς', και πιθανόν να συνδέεται με τη λέξη 'σουρ' που σημαίνει 'θωρακισμός' ή 'προστασία'. Το όνομα Σουρήν χρησιμοποιείται ως προστάτης των Χριστιανών στον Καύκασο.

in_latin.long_meaning: Suren is a name originating from the Caucasus, meaning 'armor' or 'shield', possibly derived from the word 'sur' meaning 'to armor' or 'to protect'. The name Suren serves as a patron saint for Caucasian Christians.

Prince Suren I, who came to power after the Roman emperor Constantine's recognition of Christianity, adopted the Christian faith and ruled as a Christian king.

historical_references.reference: Suren II, also known as Shapur, was the last independent ruler of the Kingdom of Armenia from 320 to 367 AD. He embraced Christianity around 325 AD during a visit to Constantinople.
historical_references.context: The Kingdom of Armenia, located in present-day Armenia and eastern Turkey, was one of the first Christian states. Suren II, who came to power after a period of political instability, converted to Christianity during a visit to Constantinople, thus solidifying the Christian faith in the kingdom.
